newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Nov 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Nov 28.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on November 28:
LOS ANGELES - A federal judge temporarily blocked enforcement of California's ballot initiative to dismantle affirmative action.

WASHINGTON - The board of trustees of the University of the District of Columbia has decided to ask for the resignation of President Tilden LeMelle, who vowed to reform the university but instead has presided over a grave financial crisis.
WASHINGTON - The Clinton administration proposed tough new air pollution standards that would affect communities, motorists and industries nationwide.

WASHINGTON - Washington Mayor Marion Barry said he is seriously considering slashing the pay of thousands of unionized city employees by six percent and cutting hundreds of jobs next month to help cover a shortfall in the district's budget.
NEW YORK - A federal judge has ruled that most investors who traded on the Nasdaq Stock Markets in the early 1990s can be represented in a massive antitrust case.

MOSCOW - Seen from the inside, the Russian economy looks frighteningly unstable with millions of workers unpaid for months, rampant tax evasion, industry stuck in a depression-size slump, and unchecked corruption and crime. But from the outside, the view is brighter.
